test_window.evidence: No date/time column in any file. Train id 0..629999, test id 630000..899999 form one contiguous block, i.e. a single row-ordered split of one generated table (630K/270K = 70/30). No group/entity key exists that could induce a disjoint-group split (no student/school/cohort id; every column is a demographic or habit attribute). 0 duplicate rows ignoring id, 0 nulls in train and test, identical column sets apart from the target.

split_policy.scheme: shuffled KFold (5-fold) on rows; no stratification needed for a continuous target, optional binned-target stratification for fold-variance stability given n=630K
split_policy.forbidden: none mandated by structure; do NOT introduce time-based or group-based splits (no time or group key exists). Any fold scheme must stay fixed across all members so OOF blending is honest.

metric.name: R2
traps: R2 = 1 - MSE/Var(y); monotone in MSE, so train with plain L2/RMSE objective — no metric-specific objective needed.

Denominator is the evaluated set's own variance, so R2 is not comparable across folds with differing target variance: aggregate as pooled-OOF R2 over the concatenated out-of-fold vector, not as a mean of per-fold R2.

Playground regressions of this shape sit at high R2 where real differences are 1e-4..1e-5; Dirichlet/random blend-weight search has approximation error of that same magnitude and can eat the gain. Use the NNLS closed form for weights (RMSE-family metric).

Target is censored: exam_score in [19.599, 100.0] with a hard mass at the 100.0 ceiling. Unclipped predictions above 100 or below the train min are strictly wasted MSE — clip inside the metric function so every blend candidate is scored post-clip.
n_test = 270K makes leaderboard noise small relative to CV noise; trust pooled OOF over single-submission deltas.

external_data.rationale: config.yaml special_rules permit external data, but no whitelist source is joinable: the whitelist keys are country, country x year, country x date, currency x month. The official data has no country, region, currency, date, or any other geographic/temporal key, and none is derivable from the 11 feature columns (age, gender, course, study_hours, class_attendance, internet_access, sleep_hours, sleep_quality, study_method, facility_rating, exam_difficulty). Whitelist rule (1) — join keys must exist in or be derivable from the official data — therefore fails for every source. The target is an individual-level exam score driven by the provided habit/demographic covariates, not by macro indicators.

data_level: Ordinal-encode the three genuinely ordered categoricals rather than one-hot: sleep_quality (poor<average<good), facility_rating (low<medium<high), exam_difficulty (easy<moderate<hard). Ordering is semantic, derivable without EDA.
Keep internet_access as a 0/1 binary; gender (3), course (7), study_method (5) are nominal and low-cardinality — feed GBDT native categorical handling and/or one-hot for linear members.

Pairwise crosses on the plausible effect-modifier pairs: study_hours x exam_difficulty, study_hours x study_method, class_attendance x study_method, sleep_hours x sleep_quality, course x exam_difficulty. Cheap at this cardinality (<=35 levels each).
Continuous interactions/ratios: study_hours * class_attendance (effective study exposure), study_hours / sleep_hours, and a deviation-from-group-mean of study_hours within course x exam_difficulty.

CV-safe target encoding for the nominal categoricals (fit inside the fold), as an alternative encoding lane to native-categorical — cardinality is low so the expected gain is small, race it rather than assume it.
age has only 8 distinct integer values (17..24): treat both as numeric and as categorical in separate lanes.
model_level: L2 / squared-error objective throughout (R2 is affine in MSE).
Clip predictions to the train target support [19.599, 100.0] as post-processing implemented INSIDE the metric function, so every tree-search node and blend candidate is evaluated post-clip.
GBDT trio with native categorical support (LightGBM / CatBoost / XGBoost) as the backbone; CatBoost is the natural favourite given 7 categorical columns.

TASK-BLEND-DECOR: the blend pool will be variance-dominated (deep GBDTs). Add one shallow, heavily regularized, different-library member (ridge/ElasticNet on one-hot + splines, or a shallow depth-3 GBDT) purely as a decorrelator before optimizing weights.
Optimize blend weights with the NNLS closed form on the OOF matrix, not Dirichlet random search — approximation error is the same order as the real gain at this R2 level.

Given a synthetic generative process over few, mostly low-cardinality features, a well-tuned single GBDT will be close to the ceiling; budget should go to encoding lanes and blend hygiene rather than exotic architectures.
A small MLP / TabM-style member on one-hot+standardized numerics is a cheap diversity source for the blend if budget allows.

partial_task_priors.reason: 7 of 11 features are categorical (gender, course, internet_access, sleep_quality, study_method, facility_rating, exam_difficulty) and age is discrete over 8 values, so encoding matters — but all are low-cardinality (<=7 levels), and 3 continuous features remain, with study_hours the dominant predictor per config notes (r=0.76). Trigger says 'all or nearly all categorical, incl. high-cardinality'; neither the exclusivity nor the high-cardinality condition holds, so the prior's claim that 'encoding is the whole game' is downgraded to 'encoding is one raced lane'.
